title: The sovereign state system
summary: A system of sovereign states developed in Europe, culminating at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, after which interference in other states' governing prerogatives became illegitimate. Medieval popes, emperors, kings and nobles had lacked supreme authority within a territory. The form spread worldwide over three centuries. With the decline of European colonial empires in the mid-20th century, the state became the only polity ever to cover the globe's entire land surface.

where.historical_name: Münster, Prince-Bishopric of Münster, Holy Roman Empire

importance.justification: The sovereign state became the form of polity covering all the world's land.

related.because: Devastation from the Thirty Years War compelled European polities to negotiate mutual recognition and sovereign autonomy at Westphalia.
Reformation conflicts fractured unified ecclesiastical authority, necessitating a decentralized territorial settlement between Catholic and Protestant rulers.

sources.title: Treaty of Westphalia

reviewer_note: How much of this was settled at Westphalia, and how much later, is debated. The pin marks Münster, where treaties were concluded.
